title: A screen in the neighbourhood
description: Entirely fictional interview with Naledi, an imagined community cinema organiser in Johannesburg. All people, events, and dialogue are invented for this demo.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: What does a neighbourhood screening offer that watching alone cannot?

turns.speaker: Naledi
turns.text: A screening gives us a reason to sit together. The conversation after the film is as important as the film itself. People stay to exchange their own stories.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Could you keep these screenings free next year?

turns.speaker: Naledi
turns.text: We can keep the screenings free, but only if the hall remains available without a rental fee. If that changes, we will need a different plan.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Someone suggested replacing the discussion with a ticketed reception. Would you support that change?

turns.speaker: Naledi
turns.text: No, I would not support that. The discussion should be open to everyone who comes to the film.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: What would you like a new visitor to know?

turns.speaker: Naledi
turns.text: You do not need to be a film expert. Come with a question, and make room for someone else's answer.
